problem: Solve the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=8$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘},$ rounded to the nearest integer.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14040762/assets/6e2223a7dadd9aeddad0b029bf2ba8fc18bafc74dcaca88346ee2b702029b597.png)

The graph above shows the curve $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ and the line $y=-\sqrt{3}.$  Find the $x$-coordinate of the point $B.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The $y$-values of both functions are the same at the intersection point. Equating the two equations gives:

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡x=-\sqrt{3}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(-\sqrt{3})=-\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

This value lies inside $-\pi \le x<\pi $, hence, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=-\frac{\pi }{3}.$ This is the $x$ coordinate of $A.$

To get another solution, we add $\pi $ to the principal value. Thus,

$$
{x}_{2}=\pi +x=\pi -\frac{\pi }{3}=\frac{2\pi }{3}.
$$

So, the $x$-coordinate of $B$ is  $\frac{2\pi }{3}.$
